title: Free generation on the inverse image of a second section-ring chart
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], $S$ its section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], $d>0$, $s\in S_d$, $U\subseteq X$ open, and $s|_U$ a free generator [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Let $\rho:S_{(s)}\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ satisfy $\rho(a/s^m)(s^m)|_U=a|_U$ for every $m\geq0$ and $a\in S_{md}$. Let $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}S_{(s)}$ induce $\rho$ under the canonical identifications [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], and put $g=\iota_s\circ q$ [def-pc-proj]. For every $e>0$ and $t\in S_e$, let $W\subseteq X$ be the ambient image of $g^{-1}D_+(t)$. The restriction $t|_W$ is a free generator of $L^{\otimes e}|_W$. Equivalently, on every subopen $V\subseteq W$, multiplication by $t|_V$ is a bijection $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(V,L^{\otimes e})$. No numerator or quotient equation on the second chart is asserted.

proof.text: Identify the ambient second-chart preimage W with X.basicOpen(ρ(t^d/s^e)). Use Proj.awayι_preimage_basicOpen, basicOpen_eq_of_affine and Scheme.preimage_basicOpen_top. Evaluating hq at the localization element identifies the pulled-back section with U.topIso.inv(ρ(t^d/s^e)); U.ι_image_basicOpen_topIso_inv identifies its ambient image.

proof.text: Reuse nonvanishing_power from SectionRingProjPreimageForward through a proof-only import all. Its already proved isomorphism transport, tensor nonvanishing, section-ring multiplication component and positive-power induction show that nonvanishing(s^n)=nonvanishing(s) for n>0. Do not duplicate those four helpers.

proof.text: For x in W, hs implies s generates at x, hence s^e is nonvanishing at x. Apply hρ to n=e and ξ=t^d, transporting d*e=e*d. The scalar ρ(t^d/s^e) is invertible on its basic open. Intersect this basic open with a generating neighbourhood of s^e; restrict the quotient equation there and use IsFreeGenerator.units_smul. This proves that t^d generates at x. Positive-power invariance with d>0 then shows that t generates at x.
